statusText: Mapped policy state: STRONG_BLOCK_NO_NEW_RISK. The latest independently verified NQ evidence remains strongly downside-biased, with a fresh Strong Sell technical snapshot inside the hour and rates/oil pressure still elevated.
recommendation: High Tail reflects verified persistent downside structure rather than scheduled-event importance alone. A durable reclaim, deeper retracements and broader two-way rotation would support de-escalation; renewed extension or shallow failed rebounds would preserve the restrictive state.
headline: Fresh Strong Sell NQ structure keeps Tail high ahead of the U.S. data and cash-open cluster.
body: At 09:25 UTC Reuters had Nasdaq 100 e-minis down 1.01%. A 11:16 UTC Investing.com technical snapshot remained Strong Sell with RSI 28.6, MACD -109.7, ADX 56.7 and negative Highs/Lows. U.S. 10Y was near 5.12% and Brent above $100. Shared Finviz context was stale and excluded.

lookbackSummary: Tail rose through the September 23 selloff, normalized overnight, then rebuilt from low/watch to high as September 24 downside efficiency persisted. The prior hourly assessments are preserved without hindsight.
outlookSummary: Current Tail remains high on fresh verified downside structure and aligned rates/oil pressure. The 12:30-15:15 UTC data/open cluster is the main near-term checkpoint; later Tail remains conditional on actually observed retracement quality, session-extreme holding and directional efficiency.

forecast.analysis: The 12:30 UTC international-transactions and weekly-claims releases, followed by Hammack at 12:50, create a high-stress checkpoint. Tail reaches 49% only if the observed post-release path continues lower with shallow rebounds, failed retracements or repeated extension.

The 13:30 UTC U.S. cash open is followed by New Residential Sales at 14:00 UTC and Paulson remarks at 14:10 UTC. High Tail is conditional on the actual opening/data path showing repeated extension, weak rebounds or session-extreme holding; two-way absorption would argue lower.

Through 15:00 UTC, high Tail requires the actual data/opening sequence to remain directionally efficient. If early extensions are substantially retraced or session extremes fail to hold, the expected path de-escalates from the high band.

By 16:00 UTC, elevated Tail is conditional on the opening move remaining unresolved. Wider rotations, deeper counter-moves or declining cross-asset pressure would favor a shift toward a more balanced regime.

At 17:00 UTC, elevated Tail requires persistent directional progress after the morning catalyst cluster. Repeated full retracements or a stable intraday range would reduce mean-reversion-failure risk.

At 18:00 UTC, the forecast assumes some normalization unless fresh directional evidence appears. Continued session-extreme holding and failed rebounds would keep Tail elevated; balanced swings would support further de-escalation.
At 19:00 UTC, Tail is in WATCH conditionally. A renewed late-session trend leg could preserve caution, while repeated two-way rotations would indicate that the earlier one-way structure has weakened.
At 20:00 UTC, WATCH reflects residual path risk rather than an assumed continuation. Persistent extremes or renewed extension would keep Tail elevated; deeper retracements would favor normalization.

At 21:00 UTC, the forecast expects lower directional efficiency absent a new catalyst. Tail remains WATCH only if the U.S. afternoon develops another sustained one-way leg with poor retracement quality.
At 22:00 UTC, Tail falls to the low band in the base case as the main U.S. catalyst window passes. A late-session breakout with failed pullbacks would invalidate that normalization.
At 23:00 UTC, the base case remains low Tail if U.S. trading closes with meaningful retracements and no unresolved directional second leg. Stress can remain high even as path risk recedes.

At 00:00 UTC, the overnight transition is expected to reduce immediate path persistence unless U.S. closing momentum carries into Asia. New extension without retracement would be the main upside risk to Tail.
At 01:00 UTC, low Tail assumes orderly overnight price discovery and no fresh geopolitical discontinuity. Persistent directional carry from the U.S. close would argue for a higher path-risk state.
At 02:00 UTC, the base case is normal two-way overnight structure. Tail would rise only if Asia produces repeated extension, shallow pullbacks and cross-asset confirmation.
At 03:00 UTC, low Tail assumes no new catalyst converts the overnight session into a one-way move. Stable yields, oil and index breadth would reinforce normalization.
At 04:00 UTC, the forecast remains low Tail but watches for Europe-open repricing. A directional break that holds near new extremes with weak retracements would raise the path-risk case.
At 05:00 UTC, European participation can amplify overnight moves. Tail remains low unless cross-asset pressure aligns with persistent NQ extension and failed counter-moves.
At 06:00 UTC, low Tail assumes European trading remains rotational. A new sustained trend with aligned rates, oil and semiconductors would increase conditional risk.
At 07:00 UTC, WATCH begins to rebuild ahead of the next U.S. session only if Europe hands off a directional structure rather than a balanced range.
At 08:00 UTC, conditional Tail rises modestly as U.S. premarket participation increases. The key distinction is whether any overnight move shows meaningful retracements or persistent extension.
At 09:00 UTC, WATCH reflects greater premarket sensitivity to yields, oil and technology breadth. A balanced range would cap Tail; aligned one-way pressure would raise it.
At 10:00 UTC, the forecast enters a higher-stress pre-data phase ahead of the 12:30 UTC durable-goods release. Tail remains WATCH unless actual price structure becomes persistently one-way.
drivers: Durable-goods release at 12:30 UTC on Sep 25

forecast.analysis: At 11:00 UTC, WATCH persists ahead of the 12:30 UTC durable-goods checkpoint. The event itself raises Stress, while Tail would require observed extension, weak retracements or session-extreme holding.
